newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.

text.p: South African bonds shrugged off a worse-than-expected February trade balance to finish slightly stronger on Thursday.
South African Revenue Services figures released earlier showed the country recorded a trade deficit of 452 million rand in February from a 517 million rand surplus in January.
The figure was well below the most pessimisic forecast of a 500 million rand surplus and 1.5 billion rand below a consensus forecast of a 1.04 billion rand surplus.

After initially kicking up to an intraday high of 15.17 percent immediately after the trade data was released at 1400 GMT, the R150 retraced gradually throughout the afternoon to settle at 15.13 percent at 1400 GMT.
"The guys were expecting the figures to be worse than expected and went into the figure short," a trader said.
Another trader said the looming long-weekend also prompted players to go short. "They did not want big positions over the weekend," he said.
Other traders felt the market had not reacted negatively to the figure as it had been leaked earlier and therefore discounted.
On Wednesday rumours did the rounds of a half-a-billion deficit. A Customs and Excise official said that he was unaware of any leaks of the data.

"I do not know from where it could have been leaked," said Chris Barnard, director of operational systems at Customs and Excise, noting that only four people had access to the data before its official release.
Volume on the market was thin on the day, with most of the major players already on holiday.
Activity was expected to pick up again next week, particularly as there were positive expectations of money supply and private sector credit extention data as well as reserves figures.
Both sets of data are due for release from next Wednesday.

One trader noted that despite the trade data, February CPI data had come in as expected at 0.5 percent month-on-month, and provided U.S. bond yields did not rise above the key 7.00 percent over the weekend, local yields would head lower next week.
On the currency market, the rand ended a lugubrious day little changed after trading in a 4.4150 to 4.4230 bid range.
At 1400 GMT it was pegged at 4.4215/4245 against the dollar from 4.4225/4255 overnight.

"The market didn't really want to do anthing today even with the bad trade figures," a trader said, adding that the rand appeared to be capped fairly aggressively at both ends of its range on the day.
"It could suggest that the Reserve Bank was in," he said, noting that the central bank is keen to reduce its high forward book exposure.
Dealers said that in the week aead the rand looked set to test below the 4.41 level on the back of a string of positive factors.

They pointed to the sale of a 30 percent stake in telecommunications parastatal Telkom to a consortium of SBC Communications Inc and Telekom Malaysia Bhd for $1.261 billion as one of the main factors boosting sentiment.
A spate of reports on the attractiveness of the rand as a high yielder was also contributing to the improved mood, they said.
Against the crosses, the rand was last at 7.1882/2008 against sterling and 0.3799/3805 marks.
Money market rates remained within their recent ranges with three-month deposit rates quoted steady at 16.50 to 16.55 percent offered and the 90-day BA rate at between 15.90 to 16.10 percent.
The Reserve Bank said the money market shortage dipped below the 10 billion rand level on Wednesday, falling to 9.850 billion rand from 10.295 billion rand on Tuesday.
The Bond Exchange said foreigners were net buyers of 480.64 million rand's worth of bonds on Wednesday after buying 359.56 million the day before.
Nominal cumulative volumes on Wednesday were pegged at 8.12 billion rand from 6.54 billion rand previously.
-- Paul Richardson, Johannesburg newsroom 27 11 482 1003
